text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The leader of leftist junior coalition partner Bulent Ecevit, says he is working in complete harmony with conservative prime minister Mesut Yilmaz.
- Parliament is expected to vote on a secularist education bill by the end of Friday.
MILLIYET
- Deputies have shelved the lifting of the parliamentary immunities of two deputies accused of being involved in a security scandal linking the state with organised crime.
- Acting head of the privatisation board says the sell-off of Turk Telecom will be speeded up.
HURRIYET
- Women MPs protested Islamists deputies blocking a bill to outlaw domestic violence.
- The number of tourists coming to Turkey increased by 10.86 percent in the first seven months of 1997.
YENI YUZYIL
- Turkish intelligence say separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerillas trained in Greece are responsible for forest fires in coastal resorts of Turkey.
CUMHURIYET
- The new goverment has not taken out religious and racially discriminatory material found in school books as part of their education reforms.
RADIKAL
- The election board says Turkey will be ready for elections by February.
DUNYA
- Turkish gold stock exchange is to launch futures trading on Friday.
ZAMAN
- Turkey is under tight security on Friday in expectation of attacks by the PKK to mark the 13th anniversary of its first bloody attack.
